cases.description: The NumericIndicator under test wraps a ConstantIndicator(3). Since 3 < 5, the UnderIndicatorRule returned by isLessThan should be satisfied at index 0.
Both the NumericIndicator under test and the other indicator return the same value (3). UnderIndicatorRule uses a strict < comparison, therefore the rule must not be satisfied.
The NumericIndicator under test returns 3 while the other indicator returns 2. Because 3 is not less than 2, the rule must be unsatisfied.
Using a multi‑index series: the NumericIndicator returns values [3,4] (index 0 → 3, index 1 → 4) and the other indicator returns 5 for every index. At index 1, 4 < 5, so the rule must be satisfied.
At index 1 the NumericIndicator returns 4 and the other indicator also returns 4. Equality does not satisfy UnderIndicatorRule, therefore the rule must be unsatisfied.
NumericIndicator wraps ConstantIndicator(-2). Since -2 < -1, the UnderIndicatorRule should be satisfied at index 0.
Both the NumericIndicator and the other indicator return 0. Equality does not satisfy UnderIndicatorRule, therefore the rule must be unsatisfied.
NumericIndicator wraps ConstantIndicator(-0.5). Since -0.5 < 0, the rule must be satisfied at index 0.
NumericIndicator wraps ConstantIndicator(2.4). 2.4 is less than 2.5, so the rule should be satisfied at index 0.
NumericIndicator wraps ConstantIndicator(2.5). Equality does not satisfy UnderIndicatorRule, therefore the rule must be unsatisfied.
Series close prices are [1,2,3]; NumericIndicator wraps ClosePriceIndicator(series). At index 0 the value is 1, which is less than 2, so the rule is satisfied.
Using the same series, at index 2 the close price is 3, which is not less than 2; the rule must be unsatisfied.
NumericIndicator wraps ConstantIndicator(1000000). Since 1,000,000 < 2,000,000, the rule should be satisfied at index 0.
Passing a null Indicator to isLessThan should result in a NullPointerException according to the contract of UnderIndicatorRule.

input.value: ConstantIndicator(5) built from a different BarSeries than the NumericIndicator under test

cases.description: UnderIndicatorRule requires both indicators to be based on the same BarSeries. Supplying an Indicator that references a different BarSeries should cause the constructor to throw an IllegalArgumentException.
